messages:
Ana_Sales: FYI demo with ZephyrHealth just failed during streaming POC — client sees truncated JSON and SSE disconnects after ~18s. Vijay on their side reports 502/resets.
Vijay_Zephyr: Yep, reproducing. We open stream, get a few events, then client JSON.parse fails: 'Unexpected end of JSON input'. Nginx logs show connection reset after chunked response.
Mike_Eng: looking now. Can you paste the exact curl/SDK call you used?
Vijay_Zephyr: curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-demo&client_id=zephyr-demo'
Mike_Eng: thx. initial hypothesis: something between client and our CDN (their nginx) is buffering/coalescing chunks or closing idle connections. That would explain mid-object truncation on their parser.
Kat_SRE: nginx default proxy_buffering can coalesce SSE frames into larger TCP writes; if their client parses per-chunk it's brittle. Recommend disabling proxy buffering for SSE endpoints. Example: 
```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass https://redwood-gateway;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection '';
}
```
Also consider `proxy_read_timeout` increase.
Ivan_SDK: Another angle — our JS SDK buffers by newline or explicit event boundaries. If their client treats every incoming TCP chunk as a complete event, it will fail when objects split. Ask them to switch to a streaming JSON decoder or use our SDK helper which collects until a full JSON payload is seen.
Vijay_Zephyr: They use an internal custom client that JSON.parse's each 'data:' chunk. Not robust, agreed. We can change it but want server-side mitigations for the demo.
Mike_Eng: Server-side quick mitigations we can do immediately: 1) ensure each SSE event is terminated with an extra newline so proxies are more likely to flush complete events, 2) add periodic keepalive events every 10s to prevent some proxies from closing the connection, 3) if necessary emit a small chunk with a complete JSON envelope per event. I'll open a tiny rollback-safe change to add an explicit `

` after data payloads.
Kat_SRE: Also check whether the gateway returned any 429s before the reset. If the gateway rate limiter triggers a hard close, some clients will see reset with partial chunks. Look for X-RateLimit-Remaining / Retry-After. We'll enable debug headers for that client id.
Ana_Sales: Quick commercial note — Zephyr asked about costs for long-lived streams. If we recommend persistent streams for production, we should propose Dedicated (reserved capacity) to prevent hitting shared rate limits. I'll capture that for the pricing follow-up.
Vijay_Zephyr: For the demo we only need ~30 concurrent streams, production could hit ~300. Will that change recommendations?
Mike_Eng: 30 is fine for hosted with the fixes; 300 is where we'd recommend reserved capacity to guarantee concurrency and avoid throttles. I'll add notes to the ticket.
Deploy-bot: deployment started: patch add-sse-terminator (commit abc123) -> staging. ETA ~10m.
Vijay_Zephyr: Testing now against staging after your patch. Looks better — events arrive continuously and the JS parser no longer errors. Running a 5min soak.
Kat_SRE: Great. After soak, we'll provide a short runbook for their infra team: disable proxy_buffering for SSE, increase proxy_read_timeout, and ensure any edge LB doesn't force-close idle keepalives.
Ana_Sales: Perfect — marking as in-progress. I'll coordinate a quick call with Zephyr to walk through infra changes and send a pricing note re: Dedicated capacity for 300+ streams. :thumbsup:
Mike_Eng: I'll follow up with a small b/patch to add explicit heartbeat event and confirm there's no perf regression.
Vijay_Zephyr: Confirmed soak passed. Thanks everyone!
